newsitem.title: NEPAL: Twists and turns in Nepal's multi-party democracy.
newsitem.headline: Twists and turns in Nepal's multi-party democracy.

text.p: Nepal's communists made a bid to form a government on Monday and said they controlled enough votes with allies in parliament to rule for the second time since multi-party democracy was launched seven years ago.
Following is a chronology of major political events since 1990:

April 8, 1990 - King Birendra, under pressure from a pro-democracy movement launched by the centrist Nepali Congress party and the United Left Front (ULF), lifts a ban on political parties imposed by his father in 1960.

April 19 - Krishna Prasad Bhattarai is named to head an interim cabinet representing Nepali Congress, the ULF and the king's nominees. He is charged with preparing a new constitution and calling general elections.
November 9 - King Birendra promulgates a new constitution establishing a multi-party democracy under a constitutional monarchy.
May 12, 1991 - Nepal's first free elections in more than three decades are held. Nepali Congress wins a clear majority, putting the communists in the opposition.
May 29 - Girija Prasad Koirala takes office as the kingdom's first popularly elected prime minister in 30 years.
March 7, 1994 - Koirala survives a communist-backed no-confidence motion.
July 10 - Koirala, undermined within Nepali Congress, resigns after losing a key vote in parliament and recommends fresh elections.
July 11 - King Birendra dissolves parliament and orders mid-term elections for November, some 18 months ahead of schedule.

November 15 - Hung parliament emerges from Nepal's second general elections under multi-party democracy, with communist Unified Marxist-Leninist (UML) party winning greatest number of seats but falling short of majority.
November 29 - UML leader Man Mohan Adhikary is appointed first elected communist prime minister heading a minority government.

June 13, 1995 - King Birendra dissolves parliament on the recommendation of Adhikary following efforts by opposition parties to table a no-confidence motion. Fresh elections ordered for November 23. Opposition says it will challenge the decision in the Supreme Court.
August 28 - The Supreme Court overturns the dissolution of parliament.
September 10 - Adhikary resigns after he loses no-confidence motion.

September 11 - Sher Bahadur Deuba is appointed prime minister to head a centre-right coalition government linking his Nepali Congress party with the Rastriya Prajatantra Party (RPP) and Nepal Sadbhavana Party (NSP).
March 24, 1996 - Deuba survives no-confidence motion.
December 24 - Deuba defeats another UML-backed censure motion by a narrow margin of two votes.
March 6, 1997 - Deuba loses a confidence motion by two votes and resigns.
March 7 - King Birendra gives political parties until March 10 to stake claim to power.
March 9 - Nepali Congress says it will attempt to form a new government.
March 10 - Communist UML stakes a claim to power in alliance with RPP splinter faction and NSP. Nepali Congress says their bid for power appears in trouble.
